say: Traveller, a small thing. A folded message for someone out among the outlaws. I can't write the name.
You go where I cannot. A note, folded small, for one who rode out of the Nation's sight. Will you take it?
Forgive me. I have a few words for someone beyond the border, and no feet to carry them. Nothing a priest need hear.
If you pass the bandits, a letter has no friends here. Would you take it where it has some?
accepted: Any of them. They will pass it on, or they will not. Say only that it is from home. Then come back and tell me.
Put it in the hands of a bandit. The right one will hear of it. Say it came from one who has not forgotten. Come back to me.
Quietly. Any outlaw will do to start. Tell them, from the one who stayed. Then return to me.
Thank you. Do not say my name. Say only that someone at home is still praying. Then return.

say: Hold. You're carrying something that isn't a weapon. What's it?
You have a look of someone running an errand. Out with it. Whose?
Walkers don't come this way for the view. What have you got for us?
Careful with the hands. What's the folded thing?
reply: A message from someone in the Holy Nation, for a sibling who rode out.
A note from home. For one of your own.
From a Holy Nation hand. For someone who left it.
A word from the one who stayed behind.
after: Hm. Give me the thing. I will see it finds who it is for. Do not look at me like that. We have kin too.
Home. Not many of us have one to write from. Leave it. Tell them it is delivered.
A word from home. I will see it reaches the right ears. Tell your sender nothing more than that.
Aye. I know whom it is for. Say it has arrived, and keep the rest to yourself.

say: It reached them? Thank you. I can't say how much that means. Take this, and a favour owed, should you ever need one.
Then it's done. I'm in your debt, traveller. A favour owed. Take these, it isn't payment.
Delivered. My thanks. I won't forget it. Here's a little, and a favour owed for the rest.
You carried it. I'll remember that. A favour owed, and some cats, for your trouble.
Would you... if you meet one of the hive, any of them... would you say a thing? I can't. I don't know how to say it as them.
I have a small request. It's the only thing I have. Will you take it to the hive?
There's a sound that isn't there. I count the days by it. Someone in the hive should know. Will you tell them?
You walk further than I do. I mean to ask something of you. A word.
accept: Say it, and I will carry it.
I will take it to the hive.
accepted: Tell them... someone out here still counts the days by the hum, though it is not there. Say it exactly. Then come back.
Find any of the hive. Tell them a ronin still counts the days by a sound that is gone. Come and tell me they heard.
Say: someone out here still counts. That is all. Then return to me and I will know the hive knows.
Tell them I count. Tell them I do not know why. Tell them I do not stop. Then come back to me.

packages: Npc Hiver (World State- Queen is dead)
say: No-hive speaks. The hive listens. What does the no-hive carry?
A no-hive carries words. We can hear them.
The no-hive stops near the hive. The hive wonders why.
You walk like one with a task. This one does not recognise the task.
reply: A ronin out there still counts the days by the hum, though it is gone.
Someone outside the hive counts the days by a sound that is not there.
A lost one asked me to tell you he still counts.
A ronin said to tell the hive: someone out here still counts.
after: ...Counts. Alone. Without the song. The hive has heard it. The hive will keep it. Tell that one: heard.
We did not know that anyone counted. We will remember that someone does. Tell the lost one: heard.
The hive hears. The hive cannot answer. The hive does not forget. Say that: heard.
That is a hard thing to count by. We are sorry it is hard. Tell the lost one we heard.

say: Heard. They said heard. ... I don't know what I feel. It's large. Take these. And a favour owed. Is that the word? Owed.
You said it? And they answered? ... I'll remember this. A favour owed. I don't forget now. That's the only thing I do well.
Heard. ... Thank you. It's a strange thing, to be heard. Here's what I have.
They know. I'm glad. I am... glad. That's a word I didn't have. Take these, and a favour owed.
A word for the Kingdom. A Shek who still wears his horns, who is not afraid of my name. Will you carry it?
I won't ask a flatskin for many things. I ask this one. Tell a Shek of the Kingdom that I live.
You go places I can't. There's a thing I'd have said to my own people. I can't say it.
Listen, outlander. A message, spoken, not written. I won't put it on paper. Will you carry it north?
accepted: Find a Shek of the Kingdom with his horns. Say: the one with the cut name is alive and has not shamed you again. Do not say where I am. Return.
A warrior of the Kingdom. Tell him that the cast-out one lives and has not shamed him again. Not where. Come back and tell me it was heard.
Say it to a Shek who wears his horns still. The cut name lives. It has not shamed him again. Nothing more. Then return.
Quiet. Quick. Then back to me. The one with the cut name is alive, and has not shamed them again. That is all.

say: Hrm. A flatskin with a face that wants to speak.
You come with words from outside the Kingdom. Say them.
Do you carry a message? You carry it badly. Out with it.
State your purpose, flatskin. Quickly. I don't like to be kept from my post.
reply: The one with the cut name is alive. He has not shamed you again.
A Shek outside the Kingdom bid me say: the cut name lives and has not shamed you again.
A cast-out one lives. He has not shamed you again. He did not say where.
The one with the cut name lives, and has not shamed you again.
after: ...Hrm. The sand has not taken him, then. Tell him nothing. I heard nothing. Go.
A cut name. ... I thought it was dust. It is alive. Hrm. Go. I did not speak.
He is alive and has not shamed us. That is more than some of the fallen can say. Go, flatskin.
I will not ask where. I will remember that. Go.

say: You said it, and they heard? ... Hrm. A favour owed, /FLATSKIN/. A Shek pays what he owes, even a cast-out one.
Then it's delivered. I won't forget this. A favour owed. Here are cats; they aren't the debt.
Heard. ... I didn't think I'd hear that. Take this, and a favour owed. I don't offer lightly.
You carried it. I owe you, then. A favour owed. Take the cats too; they're the lesser debt.
My grandfather hid a page under the floor. Old writing, from before the Cleansing. The priests say the machines wrote only lies. I need to know what it says.
I hate the machine-folk as much as anyone. But they're the only ones who can read this page, and I have to know if it's what I think it is.
A page from the old empire. If it says what my father swore it said, then a priest lied to us. Will you have one of the skeletons read it?
I found a page in a dead pilgrim's pack. Old script. A priest would burn it and me with it. The machine-folk can read it.
accept: I will show it to one.
I will bring you their answer.
accepted: Show it to one of the machine-folk. Don't tell them where it came from. Don't let a priest see you do it.
Have a skeleton read it out, every word. I'll pray for forgiveness after. Bring me what it says.
Ask it what the page says and nothing more. I don't want its opinion, only the words.
If it says nothing, burn it. If it says something, come back and tell me. Quietly.

say: You hold a page. Do you wish me to read it?
Written material. I can parse it.
That page is old. I recognise the paper.
You have something written. Read it to me or let me read it. Choose.
reply: Read it. Every word.
What does it say?
Someone needs to know what it says.
Read it out. Nothing more.
after: It asks for kindness toward those who are not like the reader. It is short. It is not dangerous. Tell them it reads clean.
It speaks of kindness. It does not say whom to harm. I do not see why it was kept hidden. Tell them it reads clean.
I have read it. It is not a weapon. It is an old request. Tell them it was read, and it was clean.
It is a plain page. The ones who feared it were afraid of the wrong thing. Tell them it reads clean.

say: Kindness. Of course. ... Thank you. I think I knew. I needed it said by someone who couldn't be burned for hearing it. A favour owed.
Clean. It reads clean. ... I'll keep that. I owe you. A favour owed, and these for your trouble.
They read it and said nothing worse. Thank you, traveller. A favour owed.
So the page was what I hoped. Thank you. I will not say more. Here is a favour owed, and some cats.
A quiet favour, traveller. Carry word to anyone who works against the slavers, and ask no questions. Tell them a debt is paid in full.
I owe a debt I can't be seen to pay. You might. The anti-slavers would understand. Will you carry it?
A coin and a word. For someone who fights the slave markets. You never had it from me.
There's a debt on my books I want closed. Not in the ledger. In a person. Will you take word to the anti-slavers?
accepted: Tell any who work against the slavers that the debt is paid in full. Ask no questions. You never had it from me. Then come back.
Anti-slavers. Any of them. A debt is paid in full. That is all. Then return to me and tell me it was taken.
Quietly. They will understand. Say the debt is paid in full, and say no more. Return when it is done.
A debt paid in full, from one who will not give a name. Speak it, then return.

say: You have the look of someone who wants to say something and not be seen saying it. Speak.
We're listening. Be quick. The Empire has ears.
A stranger with a word. Out with it.
Don't linger. What brings you?
reply: A debt is paid in full. I was told you never had it from the giver.
A debt, paid in full. It did not come from the man who sent me.
Someone owes you nothing now. He asked me to say it was paid.
A debt is closed. Ask nothing, I was told.
after: ...A debt with no name. We take those. Say nothing. He knows.
Paid in full. We will remember it came from nowhere. Go well.
A coin with no name. Those are the best coins. Tell him he is forgiven the rest.
We will not ask who. We will remember that someone did. Go.

say: They took it? Good. ... I sleep a little better. A favour owed, traveller. Take these.
Then it's paid. I'm in your debt for carrying it. A favour owed. Here's something for the trouble.
They took it, and asked nothing. Good. A favour owed. This is only cats.
Done, then. My conscience thanks you. A favour owed, whatever that's worth in this city.
